extracted.intended_audience: aspiring local politicians / district leaders and political operatives (early-20th-century urban machine politics)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and standards for winning and holding a local political district: how to recruit and retain supporters, deliver patronage, manage reputation, and operate a political machine in an urban setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make politics your full-time business
rubrics_metrics.description: The great business of your life must be politics; 'You have to give nearly all your time and attention to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not try to mix politics and business in equal quantities; example: Tammany's experiment of having both a politician and a businessman leader per district 'wouldn't mix'—the business man attended only to his store and made trouble. Full-time attention and continuous training are required for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train continually and learn the game
rubrics_metrics.description: A reformer goes down for lack of training, while a politician 'trains all the time and knows every fine point of the game.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political success requires constant practice and awareness of the practical rules and tactics of campaigning and machine work rather than purely theoretical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study human nature and act accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: There's only one way to hold a district: 'you must study human nature and act accordin'. You can't study human nature in books.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get among the people, learn what they like and dislike, and 'approach in the right side' — practical, face-to-face knowledge of constituents beats abstract study or college training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tailored recruitment tactics for different types of supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't give the same treatment to all; 'I ain't like the patent medicine man that gives the same medicine for all diseases.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in young men by giving them opportunities that appeal to their interests (singing → Glee Club, baseball → baseball club, rowing, dancing, fighting). For 'high-toned' Citizens' Union types, use civil service examinations to draw them in and then recruit them back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be omnipresent and personally visible in the district
rubrics_metrics.description: To learn human nature you have to 'go among the people, see them and be seen..I know every man, woman, and child in the Fifteenth District.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain constant, recognizable presence so constituents feel known and connected — presence builds loyalty and name recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct, timely relief to the needy as both charity and politics
rubrics_metrics.description: Go right down among the poor families and help them in the different ways they need help; be first on the ground at fires; provide quarters, clothes, and immediate assistance rather than sending them to slow charitable societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate aid creates deep gratitude and political loyalty ('Who can tell how many votes one of these fires bring me?'). Do not defer to bureaucratic charities that investigate slowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide jobs and place supporters in employment
rubrics_metrics.description: I can always get a job for a deservin' man; 'I make it a point to keep on the track of jobs' and know employers; 'no Tammany man goes hungry in my district.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain connections with employers and contractors to secure work for followers; job-placement is a core currency of loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and use private patronage in addition to public offices
rubrics_metrics.description: When public patronage is lost, an organization needs 'an immense private patronage that keeps things going' — 'we lost the public kind ... but Tammany has an immense private patronage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate non-governmental sources of favors (contracts, contractor work, railroad jobs, private works) so the machine can survive electoral defeats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity across party lines for practical favors
rubrics_metrics.description: Politicians should cooperate with opponents on placing friends: 'Me and the Republicans are enemies just one day in the year—election day. Then we fight tooth and nail. The rest of the time it's live and let live with us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep working relationships with rival leaders so you can ask them for placements or favors when needed; partisan conflict is suspended for pragmatic exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit civil service opportunities strategically to capture opponents' recruits
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch the City Record for civil service examinations; 'take my young Cit in hand, tell him all about the good thing and get him worked up till he goes and takes an examination' so he comes back to the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use merit-entry opportunities to recruit 'high-toned' or reform-minded individuals into the machine's orbit; don't ignore administrative paths that attract opponents' supporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wasting resources on printed campaign literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't send campaign literature to older voters; 'People can get all the political stuff they want — and a good deal more, too — in the papers...You ain't goin' to gain any votes by stuffin' the letter boxes with campaign documents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal contact and direct help are more effective than mass-printed political materials; excessive literature may irritate voters and lose votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be loyal and keep promises to maintain long-term leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The politicians who make a lasting success are 'men who are always loyal to their friends, even up to the gate of State prison ... men who keep their promises and never lie.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate trustworthiness within the organization; loyalty binds followers more durably than short-term gains and punishes traitors quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'honest graft' from 'dishonest graft' and avoid criminality
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the distinction between political looters and practical politicians: 'The looter goes in for himself alone ... The politician looks after his own interests, the organization's interests, and the city's interests all at the same time.' Avoid touching the 'Penal Code Tree.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue profitable opportunities that also serve the organization and city (contracts, appointments) rather than petty theft that risks penal prosecution; honest graft is framed as mutually beneficial and lawful manipulation of opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and exploit regional and identity loyalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize local attachments (e.g., 'Brooklynites natural-born hayseeds' who remain loyal to Brooklyn issues) and how they affect behavior in broader forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor appeals and expectations to regional identities; don't assume geographic recruits will adopt citywide perspectives — local loyalties can be durable and decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the leader delivers tangible benefits or risk being deposed
rubrics_metrics.description: When the voters elect a man leader, they make an unwritten contract: 'Be faithful to us, and we'll be faithful to you.' If he doesn't 'scent out jobs' or 'show himself in all ways a true statesman,' his followers may swat him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A leader must actively secure the district's share of offices, contracts, and favors; failure to deliver material benefits dissolves support and can justify replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize contingency strategies so the organization endures setbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't panic when whipped at the polls; Tammany 'has more than one string to its bow' and remained intact after losses because of private patronage and internal cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build institutional resilience (alternate patronage channels, private favors, strong internal loyalty) so a temporary electoral defeat doesn't collapse the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose reforms (civil service) that remove patronage foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil service examinations 'are underminin' the manhood of the nation' and the civil service monster threatens to 'gobble up everything' and ruin politicians' livelihoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame reforms that limit patronage as existential threats to party organization and seek alliances (even cross-party) to resist them; treat civil service as a strategic front rather than a purely policy debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symbolic small-currency politics (children, local acts) to cement goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: The children 'know me...and they know that a sight of Uncle George and candy means the same thing. Some of them are the best kind of vote-getters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small gestures (treats for children, presence at celebrations) create emotional bonds and mnemonic loyalty that pay off at the polls.
